learning_objective: 🎯 Build a powerful word bank to make your writing and speaking sound impressive, natural, and super smart!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Using the same words over and over gets boring! Instead of saying 'good' 50 times, you can say 'excellent', 'fantastic', or 'brilliant'. A strong vocabulary makes your writing colourful and shows off your brainpower!

Synonyms are words that have the EXACT SAME or very similar meanings. They are like twins! Example: Big and Huge, Smart and Clever, Happy and Joyful. Using synonyms stops your writing from sounding repetitive.

Antonyms are words with totally OPPOSITE meanings. Example: Hot and Cold, Brave and Cowardly, Ancient and Modern. You can often make an antonym just by adding a prefix like 'un' or 'dis' (Happy -> Unhappy, Agree -> Disagree).

Collocations are words that naturally go together in English. Native speakers just know they fit! For example, we say 'Fast food' but we never say 'Quick food'. We say 'Make a mistake', not 'Do a mistake'. Learning collocations makes you sound like a native speaker!

If you see a new word and do not have a dictionary, look at the words around it! The 'context' will give you clues. If a sentence says 'The elephant is a MAMMOTH creature, much bigger than a lion', you can guess 'mammoth' means very big!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The 'Very' Ban Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Try not to use the word 'very' for one whole day! Instead of 'very tired', say 'exhausted'. Instead of 'very cold', say 'freezing'. Write down 3 new 'very' replacements you learned today.

quick_recap: ⭐ Synonyms are words with similar meanings (sad = unhappy).
⭐ Antonyms are words with opposite meanings (tall vs. short).
⭐ Collocations are word pairs that naturally sound right together (e.g., 'heavy rain' instead of 'strong rain').
⭐ Adding prefixes like un-, in-, or dis- is a quick way to create antonyms.
⭐ Use context clues from the sentence to guess the meaning of unknown words.
